prompt: Match each format with the incidental thing it also measures.

pairs.right: how much free time the candidate has
performance under pressure, and practice at that style of problem

right_distractors: how well they know the company

prompt: Which format does the lesson say is furthest from how the job is done?
hint: A bare editor, against the clock.

choices.text: The take-home, since it is done at home where nobody can see how the person really works
choices.why: It is the closest to how most engineering work is done.

choices.text: Pairing
choices.why: Much of the job is working on code with somebody else.

choices.text: They are equally far from it
choices.why: The lesson ranks live coding furthest.

choices.text: Live coding
choices.why: Right: it has the largest incidental measurements.

prompt: Why does a “two-hour” take-home often become a competition in unpaid work?
hint: What candidates expect of each other.

choices.text: Companies hide the real time limit
choices.why: Not the mechanism described.

choices.text: Because the problems are deliberately too hard to finish in the suggested time
choices.why: Some are mis-sized, which the next sections address, but the lesson’s point is the competition.

choices.text: Interviewers ask for extra features
choices.why: Not mentioned.

choices.text: Candidates spend longer because they know others will
choices.why: Right: the suggested limit stops meaning anything when everybody exceeds it.

prompt: What does pairing depend on more than the other formats?

choices.text: The candidate’s home internet connection
choices.why: Not the lesson’s point.

choices.text: The interviewer
choices.why: Right: the same hour can be collaborative or a test with an audience.

choices.text: The language chosen
choices.why: Not the point either.

choices.text: How many hours the candidate is willing to spend preparing over the weekend before the session
choices.why: That is the take-home’s incidental measurement.

prompt: Where does the lesson say the choice of format should start?

choices.text: From the job
choices.why: Right: what the role needs to show decides which incidental measurement matters least.

choices.text: From what the company has always used
choices.why: That is how most are chosen, and what the lesson argues against.

choices.text: From what candidates prefer
choices.why: Candidates’ costs matter, but the starting point is the job.

choices.text: From whatever the large technology companies are currently using for similar roles
choices.why: Copying another company’s format is habit at one remove.

prompt: What did Renata need Agenda’s technical interview to show? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Whether they already know Python
choices.why: No: Python was on the not-required list.

choices.text: Whether they write tests without being asked
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: How the person approaches an unfamiliar codebase
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: How fast they can solve an algorithm puzzle
choices.why: No: that is what live coding shows, and the job did not need it.

choices.text: How they talk through a decision with a colleague
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Why is “fixed the bug” not a row in Yara’s rubric?

choices.text: The bug is too easy
choices.why: Difficulty is not the reason.

choices.text: Because Yara fixes it herself during the session
choices.why: She pairs and suggests; she does not do the work.

choices.text: A silent fix without a test shows less of the job than a test written first and no time left to fix
choices.why: Right: the rubric scores approach, testing and collaboration, which is what the job needs.

choices.text: Fixing bugs is not part of the job
choices.why: Fixing time-zone bugs is in the first-six-months paragraph.

prompt: Why did Renata not add a take-home on top of the pairing session?
hint: Each stage has to earn its cost.

choices.text: Take-homes are illegal
choices.why: They are not; paying for them is one way to make them fairer.

choices.text: Pairing already showed what it would add, and it would cost fifteen candidates hours of unpaid work
choices.why: Right: an extra stage has to earn its cost to candidates, not only to the company.

choices.text: Yara refused to mark them
choices.why: Not in the lesson.

choices.text: They cannot show anything a pairing session cannot
choices.why: For a role of solitary long problems, the lesson says a short paid take-home might serve better.

prompt: How does the lesson suggest checking that a take-home really takes two hours?

choices.text: Ask candidates afterwards how long it took them
choices.why: Afterwards is too late, and candidates under-report.

choices.text: Put a timer in the repository that stops the candidate from committing after two hours
choices.why: Nothing like this is in the lesson.

choices.text: Have somebody on the team do it first
choices.why: Right: if the team’s engineers need four, it is a four-hour exercise.

choices.text: Trust the label
choices.why: The label is exactly what the check is for.

prompt: Why does Caju say “it is fine to think aloud, be silent, look things up and ask” to every candidate?

choices.text: Lawyers require the sentence
choices.why: No legal requirement is mentioned.

choices.text: To shorten the session
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: Because nervous candidates are usually the strongest engineers once they settle into the work
choices.why: The lesson makes no such claim; it is about equal conditions.

choices.text: So it is part of the conditions, not a kindness some candidates get
choices.why: Right: the same conditions for everybody is the point.

prompt: A candidate with dyslexia needs more time. How does Caju’s process handle it?
hint: Without the interviewers needing to know why.

choices.text: The recruiter arranges it, and interviewers do not need the reason
choices.why: Right: the invitation asks about adjustments, and the request goes through the recruiter.

choices.text: The candidate explains the diagnosis to the interviewer at the start of the session
choices.why: The process deliberately avoids that.

choices.text: No adjustment, for fairness to others
choices.why: An interview some people cannot take on equal terms measures something else; adjustments are required.

choices.text: A different, shorter problem
choices.why: More time on the same problem keeps the comparison fair.

prompt: Giving the problem in advance removes most of the cold-start ___ that live coding measures.
A company’s technical interview is a 45-minute whiteboard algorithm problem with no references, the same for every role from front-end to data. What would this lesson question first?

choices.text: Whether 45 minutes is long enough
choices.why: The length is secondary to whether the format fits the job at all.

choices.text: Whether the interviewers are senior enough
choices.why: Briefing matters, but the format choice comes first.

choices.text: Whether any of those roles needs what live coding shows more than what it measures by accident
choices.why: Right: the format was chosen by habit, not from what each job needs to show.

choices.text: Whether the problems are hard enough to separate strong candidates from weak ones
choices.why: Harder problems widen the incidental measurement, not the relevant one.
